newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to hold key coffee policy meeting Dec 19.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to hold key coffee policy meeting Dec 19.

text.p: Thailand will hold a 1997 coffee policy meeting later this week during which the commerce ministry might seek to guarantee prices paid to local planters, a commerce ministry source said on Tuesday.
The meeting, to be attended by representatives from the commerce and agriculture ministries and coffee planters, would be held on December 19, the sources told Reuters.
The meeting was originally scheduled for November 30 but was postponed after the change of government in the November 17 general election.
There were rumours earlier that the government might seek to guarantee local planters a coffee price of 30 baht ($1.20) per kg.
Thailand exported about 60,000 tonnes of coffee beans in 1995 from an estimated total output of 78,801 tonnes, according to official figures.
The agriculture ministry has forecast coffee output this year at 81,398 tonnes.
